call_site_note: No production call site exists. The three landed paths are an evidence fragment, its data JSON and a standalone script; grep for sib-dd-completion-estimate over imas_codex/ and tests/ returns nothing, and the only other references are the plan's own comment block.

findings.text: spend() adds each configured seat's own cost_per_call and multiplies that sum by the phase's whole planned call count, so a phase with three seats prices every call at triple cost. Asserted from the committed JSON: review_name 1557 calls x (0.043703 + 0.003199 + 0.075507) = 190.5908, review_docs 2468 x (0.074513 + 0.037489 + 0.044293) = 385.7361. The same seats' records over the 90-day window give a weighted mean of 0.029228 and 0.056463 USD/call (173.708/5944 and 304.232/5388), i.e. USD 45.5 and USD 139.4 for the same call counts. The headline total is therefore ~USD 664 against ~USD 273 on the measured basis, and the 1,317 high arm scales the same error; the node's central deliverable is an overstated spend figure.

The text states compose is the only phase whose call count 'comes from the queue directly', but sib-dd-completion-estimate-run.py:419-423 takes remaining from the dry run's extraction_candidates (1308) and the batches at line 333 divide that, while logs/dryrun.log:13 reports generate_name pending=1397; the queue basis is 56 batches, not the 53 reported, so the sentence's provenance claim and its number disagree.

Two distinct phases are rendered under the same 'refine' label (600 calls / USD 83.29 and 1608 calls / USD 150.08; the JSON keys are refine_name and refine_docs), and the neighbouring row keeps the raw key 'refine_name+fanout', so a reader cannot match a row to its phase without opening the JSON.

The refine projection is USD 23.56 over 6827 calls, 58 percent of all planned calls, priced entirely from gpt-6-luna's 7 observed refine_docs calls (model_costs_90d refine_docs, cost_per_call 0.003451) against 1608 refine_docs calls in that window - a 0.4 percent sample - while the bulk of the window's refine traffic ran on models the seats do not name; the caveats list at line 31-36 does not say that the largest call block carries the thinnest price sample.

justifications.durability: No test is added and the node declares negative_control none, so nothing in the repository reddens if spend() at sib-dd-completion-estimate-run.py:313 or the duplicated EXTRACTION_FILTER at line 57 regresses; the spend defect found here passed the gate precisely because of that.
justifications.evidence: logs/estimate-gate.log carries the literal command, rev eee64e7cd, the worktree path and EXIT=0, and b1191a9a5 differs from that revision only in generated_at, so the recorded result is the artifact; but the runner asserts nothing, so the gate records a successful execution rather than a check over the figures it prints.
justifications.fit: The fragment prefixes every element id with the node id and carries the plan-id/plan-section/node-id meta, matching the sibling fragments, but sib-dd-completion-estimate.html:21 renders refine_docs and refine_name under the same 'refine' label.
justifications.goal_fidelity: sib-dd-completion-estimate-run.py:313-321 sums each configured seat's cost_per_call and multiplies the sum by the phase's whole call count, so review_name reports USD 190.59 for 1557 calls (0.122409/call, the sum of grok-4.5, gpt-6-luna and sonnet-5) and review_docs USD 385.74, against weighted means of 0.029228 and 0.056463 over the same configured seats (USD 45.5 and 139.4), making the headline 664.10 about 2.4x the measured basis.
justifications.reuse: EXTRACTION_FILTER at sib-dd-completion-estimate-run.py:57-78 reproduces clause for clause the extraction predicate that imas_codex/standard_names/sources/dd.py:676 owns inside extract_dd_candidates (node_category, description, leaf invariant and signal exception, core_instant_changes, lifecycle_status), so the addition duplicates rather than extends the owner.

verdicts.text: The goal is to estimate the calls, spend and wall time to compose, document and review every remaining DD source; docs/evidence/fragments/sn-integrity-backlog/sib-dd-completion-estimate.html:6,25,27,28 report all three (11,698-23,153 calls, USD 664.0961-1,317.1691, 18.5-36.6 h), but the spend half is materially wrong because sib-dd-completion-estimate-run.py:313-321 charges every planned call at the sum of each configured seat's per-call cost, so two of the five phases overstate spend roughly 3-4x.

The done_when asks for the population by source status and name stage, the extracted-source class split, the dry-run planned calls and spend per phase, the 30-day measured per-name cost, a wall-time estimate and the runner with a log ending in EXIT=; logs/estimate-gate.log records the exact command, revision eee64e7cd, the worktree path and EXIT=0, and every element is present in the emitted JSON (population.dd_sources_by_status, names_by_stage, extracted_dd_sources.classification, estimate.arms, measured_cost_30d, throughput) - the gate is a run of the runner rather than an assertion over its numbers.

Declared paths are the three fragment files plus docs/figures/sn-integrity-backlog/sib-dd-completion-estimate; git diff --stat 2c9ea5cb..b1191a9a5 is exactly those three files, 1034 insertions and 0 deletions, with no plan file and no figure, so nothing outside the fence landed.
